study: Breakout distance above a just-broken LuxAlgo sell zone at desk-like square moments, on untouched history: do chases (>= 0.30%) do worse, and clean breaks (0.10-0.30%) better, than square moments with no breakout?
registered_at: 2026-10-06 ~18:30 ET, before any of this period's bars were fetched with lows or any order block was computed on it
origin: Operator 10/6: 'can we test the breakout distance SR flag to prove its usefulness?' Leads from order_block_gate.py (9/11-10/02, information cells): chase -21/-27 bp vs non-breakout arms (t -1.3/-1.6); clean +14.5 (t +1.5). The forward test on desk fills (sr_breakout_forward_prereg.json) stays; this is a faster check on more data.
period: sessions 2026-05-01..2026-09-10 (ends before the 9/11-10/02 sample already mined); split by date into first and second half. DISCLOSURE: this universe and period (sipbrk_min caches, 5/1-9/11, RTH, no lows) were used on 10/3 for the SIP breakout stage-1 test, whose outcomes were seen; never for order blocks or breakout distance.
universe: per session the 40 largest opening gappers: open >= $10, prior-day $vol >= $20M, gap >= +2% (sip_breakout_study.universe on ai_reports/allsym/daily_2025-09-01_2026-10-02.pkl) AND a RAW 09:30 open >= $10 from the minute bars (the daily panel is split-adjusted; a later reverse split can admit a cheap name).
bars: SIP 1-minute, RAW (unadjusted), prior trading day + the day, 04:00-16:00 ET; prior-day bars dropped when the day's first bar / prior last close is outside [0.5, 2.0] (split in the window); requested vs returned names logged per day, days under 90% flagged
events: 1-min close 09:40-15:00 ET with fast %R (21, EMA 7) >= -20 AND slow %R (112, EMA 3) >= -20 (the desk's square, approximated on SIP); first such minute per name per clock 15-min block
feature: brk = % the close is above the top of the most recently broken charted bearish OB (break within the last 15 min, close still above its top), blocks point-in-time from tools/order_blocks.py (swing 10, wicks, charted last 3 per side). Bands: none | poke [0,0.10) | clean [0.10,0.30) | chase [0.30, inf).
outcome: net15 = next bar open -> close of the last bar starting at or before entry + 15 min (~16 min), minus 0.20%; events whose exit bar is > 3 min off target are dropped and counted per band
statistic: band vs 'none' events, OLS with day fixed effects, day-clustered t

pass.H2_chase: chase minus none <= -5 bp with t <= -2 in BOTH halves, AND pooled t <= -2.24 (Bonferroni 2), >= 100 chase events per half
pass.H3_clean: clean minus none >= +5 bp with t >= 2 in BOTH halves, AND pooled t >= 2.24, >= 100 clean events per half
pass.else: fewer than 100 events in a half -> UNDERPOWERED; otherwise FAIL
pass.consequence: a PASS ranks square moments against each other; if the passing band is still net negative or below the random-minute control it is a SKIP/PRIORITY signal, not an entry edge. Live reads IEX with a 3-session window (ob_observe.py, operator override 10/6) while this is SIP with 2 sessions, so before any live A/B either a same-script rerun with feed=iex must agree in sign or the forward test (sr_breakout_forward_prereg.json) must pass; skeptic review first.

no_retuning: bands, 15-min break window, swing 10, charted-3, %R thresholds and the 15-min hold are fixed here
caveats: SIP bars; the desk sees IEX
square approximated (the desk's minute-grid %R differs slightly)
fixed 15-min hold, not the desk's trail
the 10/5 leads were picked from many cells and are likely inflated; the per-half detectable effect is ~11-12 bp, so a small true effect can FAIL
information_only: per band, event minus a same-name, same-day, same-clock-hour random-minute control (seed 31)
